answer: An oasis exchange hires agents to allocate water across a ridge and dune farms. Bidding power comes from signed valve-meter tickets, each representing a measured litre delivered last week; tickets are consumed when bids settle. Creating fifty accounts makes no new tickets. To control fifty times the allocation, an attacker must buy real water rights and operate enough metered flow, paying for both. A corrupt meter could mint fake tickets, so two independent meters reconcile totals and suspicious readings face inspection; small farms can pool tickets without pooling identities.
